  innermost body `est s 0 (eld E s 0 (lv DB) pos) (lv DR) (lv O)` and O += `lv One`; its value `lv
  R`. When every index is a scalar (a view base, rule 18 folded), its value after IX 2 is `eld E s
  0 data(B) pos`. Sites: the `idx`'s line; `range step is zero` the `rng`'s.
* **L6** (rules 21, 19 for `.flat`, 15 (i)) `asg set` to an `idx` with an index of kind R, A, V, M
  or MM or with a `view flat` base: `block P n` with:
  1. *the value*: a scalar `tmp Vv = value`; a dynamic array `bind Vv = value` (held, R8: retained
     when borrowed, rule 21 (1)); a fixed-size array `tmp Vv = value` (it names its home, R9), except
     that a value that is `lv` of the target's root variable is copied into a new home first (`tmp V0
     = value`, `tmp Vv = anew P TV 0 0`, `tmp NB = ci bytes`, `mcpy data(Vv) data(V0) (lv NB)`; a
     fixed-size target has no copy on write, LANGUAGE.md §5.5 "Aliasing", Decision 34's reasoning);
  2. *the indices*: IX 1 of the target, every index vector and mask a `tmp` (an owned one released at
     the block's end, R11), except under Decision 34: a dynamic index vector of a dynamic target
     whose element type is `i64` is `bind W = e` (held: retained when borrowed, so the target's cow
     copies a shared buffer), and on a fixed-size `i64` target an index vector that is `lv` of the
     target's root is copied into a new home first (`tmp W0 = e`, `tmp W = anew P TW 0 0`, `tmp NB =
     ci bytes`, `mcpy data(W) data(W0) (lv NB)`); no other index vector can share the target's
     storage;
  3. IX 2;
  4. for an array value, IX 3 and the shape check, the selection's shape first: a vector `tmp NV =
     ext(Vv, 0)`, `tmp S = bin ne (lv N) (lv NV)`, vchk(SHAPE_MISMATCH; S, N, NV); a matrix `tmp RV`,
     `tmp CV`, `tmp S0`, `tmp S1` (`bin ne` of each pair), `tmp S = bin bor`, mchk(SHAPE_MISMATCH; S,
     R, C, RV, CV);
  5. for a dynamic target `cow (lv T)` (a fixed-size target needs none, rule 19);
  6. `tmp DT = data(T)`, for an array value `tmp DV = data(Vv)`, the DW and DM of each index vector
     and mask, for an array value `bind O = ci 0` and `tmp One = ci 1`;
  7. IX 4 with the innermost body `est s 0 (lv Vv)` (or `(eld E s 0 (lv DV) (lv O))`, then O += `lv
     One`) `(lv DT) pos`.

  At the end of the block the owned index `tmp`s are released (R11), then the held locals in reverse
  order (the retained index vectors, then the value): rule 21 (8). An `asg set` to `.flat` with a
  scalar index is the same block without step 4 and the nest: steps 1, 2, 3, 5, then `est s 0 (lv
  Vv) data(T) (lv I)` (rule 19's order). **Compound** `asg op` (op ≠ `set`) to such a target: `block
  P n` with step 2 of the plain form (Decision 34's `bind` and copy apply: `w[w] += 10`, §6.2); `bind
  G = xblk P TG m` { IX 2–4 of L5 reading the selection into `tmp G0` with step 2's `tmp`s; `tmp Vv =
  value`; the statements of L7 for `G0 op Vv` (its shape check with G0 first) into `tmp R0`; value `lv
  R0` } (T2 releases G0 and an owned Vv right after the operation; for a fixed-size result G is a
  `tmp`, R9); then steps 3–7 storing G's elements with step 2's `tmp`s (extents and checks loaded
  again); G is released at the block's end. A compound `.flat` store with a scalar index: step 2, the
  folded read into `tmp Tv` (checks included), `tmp Vv = value`, `tmp R0 = bin op (lv Tv) (lv Vv)`
  (rule 1, the `asg`'s site), steps 3 and 5, the store. **Whole arrays**: `asg op (lv a) e` of an
  array local or `ref` parameter a is `asg set (lv a) x`, x the L7 `xblk` of `bin op (lv a) e` (rule
  15 (i); a fixed-size a stored by rule 27 (d)). Sites: the `asg`'s line for every check, `chk` and
  `cow`; `range step is zero` the `rng`'s. For §3.6.6 rule 12 the whole block is the one statement of
  the `asg` (its reads before a `ref` call are copied, the store's reads of the target are not).

* **L7** (rule 22) a `bin`, `un`, `cvt`, `powk` or elemental `lib` (LANGUAGE.md §10.1, §10.4, §10.7)
  with an array operand: `xblk P T n` with: (1) `tmp Ak = ` operand k, left to right (scalars too);
  (2) when the result is dynamic, the extents of every array operand in operand order (a vector
  `Nk = ext(Ak, 0)`, a matrix `Rk`, `Ck`), when it is fixed-size those of the matrix operands
  only; then the checks of a dynamic result: vectors, for each array operand k after the first (so none, and
  no V, with one array operand),
  `tmp S = bin ne (lv N1) (lv Nk)`, vchk(SHAPE_MISMATCH; S, N1, Nk) (its `tmp V` written at the
  first check only, after that comparison); matrices, with the combined
  shape (R, C) = (R1, C1) and each later array operand's (r, c): `tmp O = ci 1` (once), `bind a =
  bin eq (lv R) (lv r)`, `tmp b = bin eq (lv R) (lv O)`, `tmp c = bin eq (lv r) (lv O)`, `asg set
  (lv a) (bin bor (lv a) (lv b))`, the same with c, the same for the columns into `bind a2`, `asg set
  (lv a) (bin band (lv a) (lv a2))`, `tmp S = un not (lv a)`, mchk(SHAPE_MISMATCH; S, R, C, r, c),
  `tmp R' = lib where (bin eq (lv R) (lv O)) (lv r) (lv R)`, `tmp C' = ` the same for C, (R, C) :=
  (R', C'); (3) `tmp RES = anew P T 0 k` with N1 (vectors) or the final (R, C), or for a fixed-size
  T `anew P T 0 0` followed by its extents (a vector `tmp N = ext(RES, 0)`, a matrix `tmp R =
  ext(RES, 0)` and `tmp C = ext(RES, 1)`, the R and C of (4) and (6)); (4) matrices: for each
  array operand X `tmp SI = bin ne (lv rX) (lv O)`, `tmp t = bin ne (lv cX) (lv O)`, `tmp SJ = wbin
  mul (lv t) (lv rX)` (R7; `tmp O = ci 1` at its first use if (2) wrote none); (5) `tmp DR =
  data(RES)`, then `tmp Dk = data(Ak)` of each array operand in order; (6) a vector loop(N; I) {
  `est s 0 F (lv DR) (lv I)` }, a matrix mloop(R, C; I, J) { `est s 0 F (lv DR) lin(I, J, R)` },
  where F is the node itself with each array operand replaced by `eld Ek sk 0 (lv Dk) (lv I)`
  (matrix: index `wbin add (wbin mul (lv I) (lv SIk)) (wbin mul (lv J) (lv SJk))`) and each scalar
  operand by `lv Ak`; its value `lv RES`. Owned operands are temporaries of the `xblk`, released
  after the nest (T2, rule 22 (8)). Site: the node's line.
* **L8** (rule 25) a `rng` that is neither an index nor a `forr`'s range: `xblk P T n` with `tmp LO =
  lo`, `tmp HI = hi`, `tmp ST = st` (or `ci 1`), `rcnt incl L E`, `tmp O1 = ci 1`, `tmp T = wbin add
  (lv L) (lv O1)`, `tmp Z = ci 0`, `tmp N = lib where (lv E) (lv T) (lv Z)`, `tmp X = ci
  #000000007FFFFFFE` (`SEA_LIM_EXTENT` − 1 = 2 147 483 646 in the `i` encoding of §3.1), `tmp G = bin gt (lv L) (lv X)`, `tmp U = bin lt (lv L) (lv Z)`,
  `bind Bf = bin bor (lv G) (lv U)`, `asg set (lv Bf) (bin band (lv Bf) (lv E))`, `tmp MX = ci
  #7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF` (2⁶³ − 1, written as the field text, never computed: a Baysick number cannot
  hold it; 2 147 483 646 is exact), `bind Ef = bin eq (lv L) (lv MX)`, `asg set (lv Ef) (bin bor (lv Ef) (lv
  U))`, `tmp V = lib where (lv Ef) (lv MX) (lv T)`, `chk ARRAY_SIZE 1 (lv Bf) (lv V)`, `tmp A = anew P
  T 0 1 (lv N)`, `tmp D = data(A)`, `bind Q = ci 0`, `tmp One = ci 1`, rloop(E, LO, L, ST; K) { `est 8
  0 (lv K) (lv D) (lv Q)`; Q += `lv One` }; its value `lv A`. P and every site: the `rng`'s. A `for`
  over a range value (`for x in (0..n)`) is L4 over this vector.
* **L9** (rule 26 (a)–(d), numeric elements) an `arr` of type T: (a) fixed-size T without
  concatenation: `xblk P T n` with `tmp H = anew P T 0 0`, `tmp D = data(H)`, then each element in
  source order `est s 0 e (lv D) (ci k)`, k = i + j·r for element (i, j) of an r × c literal; value
  `lv H`. (b) dynamic T without concatenation: `tmp R = ci n` (one row), or `tmp R = ci r` and `tmp
  C = ci c`; `tmp A = anew P T 0 k`; `tmp D = data(A)`; when every element is a `ci`, `cf` or `cb`,
  `tmp S = cdat P ^E n` with the constants in column-major order, `tmp B = ci bytes`, `mcpy (lv D)
  (lv S) (lv B)`; otherwise each element in source order `est s 0 e (lv D) (ci k)`; value `lv A`.
  (c) concatenation: `tmp Qk = ` part k in source order (scalar parts too); then the shapes, row by
  row, each row's join before its stack check: a row of scalars and vectors `tmp L1 = ext(Q1, 0)` (a
  scalar `tmp L1 = ci 1`), then for each later part its length `tmp Lk` and `tmp Nk = wbin add` of
  the sum so far and Lk, with no check (a vector row; in a stack it counts as (`tmp = ci 1`, its sum));
  a row of matrices and scalars (Rr, Cr) = the first part's extents (a scalar two `tmp = ci 1`), then
  for each later part its (Rk, Ck), `tmp S = bin ne (lv Rr) (lv Rk)`, mchk(SHAPE_MISMATCH; S, Rr, Cr,
  Rk, Ck), `tmp Cr' = wbin add (lv Cr) (lv Ck)`; the stack (Rs, Cs) = the first row's, then after each
  later row's join `tmp S = bin ne (lv Cs) (lv Ck)`, mchk(SHAPE_MISMATCH; S, Rs, Cs, Rk, Ck), `tmp Rs'
  = wbin add (lv Rs) (lv Rk)`; `tmp RES = anew P T 0 k` (a vector result, one row of scalars and vectors: the sum; a matrix
  result: Rs, Cs, for a single row of matrices its Rr, Cr); `tmp DR =
  data(RES)`; then each part in source order at its offsets, each offset a `tmp` (a first offset
  `tmp = ci 0`, a later one `tmp = wbin add` of the previous offset and the previous part's length or
  extent; r0 per row, c0 per part within its row): in a vector result a scalar part `est s
  0 (lv Qk) (lv DR) (lv c0)` and a vector part `tmp Dq = data(Qk)`, loop(Lk; I) { `est s 0 (eld E s 0
  (lv Dq) (lv I)) (lv DR) (wbin add (lv c0) (lv I))` }; in a matrix result a scalar part
  `est s 0 (lv Qk) (lv DR) lin(r0, c0, Rs)`, and a matrix part, or a vector part of a row of the stack
  (its Rq a `tmp = ci 1`, its Cq its length), `tmp Dq = data(Qk)`, mloop(Rq, Cq; I, J) { `est s 0 (eld
  E s 0 (lv Dq) lin(I, J, Rq)) (lv DR) (wbin add (wbin add (lv r0) (lv I)) (wbin mul (wbin add (lv
  c0) (lv J)) (lv Rs)))` }; value `lv RES`. When every part is fixed-size: `anew P T 0 0`, no checks
  (their `tmp S` and `mchk` dropped), but the length and extent sums (`tmp Nk = wbin add`, `tmp Cr'`,
  `tmp Rs'`) still written, the parts' extents their `ext` (`li`), and every offset a `tmp = ci` of its static value (an `li`;
  never a constant index child, which R3 would fold). The parts are the `xblk`'s first `tmp`s, so T2
  releases the owned ones after the copies in part order. (d) `[]`: `anew P T 1 k` with `ci 0`
  children (dynamic T), `anew P T 0 0` (fixed-size T). Site: the `arr`'s line.

* **L10** (rule 28 materialized, rule 27 (i), (j)) a `view` that is not an `idx` base: `.flat`,
  `.col`, `.row`: `xblk P T n` with `tmp A = ` the operand, for a dynamic operand `tmp R = ext(A,
  0)` (`.flat` also `tmp C = ext(A, 1)` and `tmp N = wbin mul (lv R) (lv C)`), `tmp V = anew P T 0
  k` (`.flat` N; `.col` R and `ci 1`; `.row` `ci 1` and R) or `anew P T 0 0` (fixed-size), `tmp D =
  data(V)`, `tmp S = data(A)`, `tmp NB = wbin mul (count) (ci s)` (fixed-size: `ci bytes`), `mcpy (lv
  D) (lv S) (lv NB)`, value `lv V`; `.T`: `tmp A`, `tmp R = ext(A, 1)`, `tmp C = ext(A, 0)`, `tmp V =
  anew P T 0 2 (lv R) (lv C)` (fixed-size: `anew P T 0 0`), `tmp DV = data(V)`, `tmp DA = data(A)`,
  mloop(R, C; I, J) { `est s 0 (eld E s 0 (lv DA) lin(J, I, C)) (lv DV) lin(I, J, R)` }, value `lv V`.
  Site: the `view`'s line. `dyn`: `tmp S = ` the operand, `tmp R = ext(S, 0)` (and `tmp C =
  ext(S, 1)`: `li` of the static extents), `tmp A = anew P T 0 k`, `tmp D = data(A)`, `tmp N = ci
  bytes`, `mcpy (lv D) data(S) (lv N)`, value `lv A`. `fix`: `tmp A = ` the operand; a vector `tmp R
  = ext(A, 0)`, `tmp En = ci n`, `tmp S = bin ne (lv R) (lv En)`, vchk(SHAPE_EXPECTED; S, En, R); a
  matrix `tmp R`, `tmp C`, `tmp Er = ci r`, `tmp Ec = ci c`, `tmp S0 = bin ne (lv R) (lv Er)`, `tmp S1
  = bin ne (lv C) (lv Ec)`, `tmp S = bin bor`, mchk(SHAPE_EXPECTED; S, Er, Ec, R, C); then `tmp H =
  anew P T 0 0`, `tmp D = data(A)`, `tmp N = ci bytes`, `mcpy data(H) (lv D) (lv N)`, value `lv H`
  (an owned A released by T2). Sites: the node's line.
* **L11** (Decision 33) `ind2sub(r, k)` with a scalar `r` and an array `k` (an array `r` is the
  phase-rule word `ind2sub` until phase 6, §2.6.2), of type `(T1, T2)`; P is the position of the `lib
  ind2sub` (every node L11 writes takes it); with one array operand there is no shape check: for
  `tbind (I, J)`, in place of the `tbind` in its block (not a block of its own: the `tbind` declares
  I and J for the rest of the enclosing block, LANGUAGE.md §7.7): `bind R' = r` (a scalar `.l` local, rule 2), then k: a dynamic
  array `bind K' = k` (held, rule 30 (1)), a fixed-size one `tmp K' = k` (naming its home, R9), `bind I = ` the L7 `xblk` of `bin mod (lv K') (lv R')`,
  `bind J = ` the L7 `xblk` of `lib idiv (lv K') (lv R')` (for a fixed-size result a `tmp`, R8; a `_`
  component is an `eval` of its L7 `xblk`, whose owned value rule 15 (h) releases right after it),
  the block's n growing by 3; for `tasg` and `tret`,
  a new `block P n` with the same statements, I and J new `.l` locals (`bind`, or `tmp` for
  fixed-size results, R8) followed by the stores of rule 15 (j) in target order (`asg
  set` of `lv I`, `lv J`) or by `ret 2 (lv I) (lv J)`. The held locals are released at the end of
  their block (rule 16); for `tbind` that is the enclosing block, so a held K' outlives the
  statement (a `block` of its own would end the scope of I and J, and `sea.hirl` has no release
  record): only its memory lives longer, nothing a program can observe. The two loops report the error a single loop would (`integer division by
  zero` at element 0 of the first loop for r = 0; an `idiv` overflow at its element), so the output
  cannot differ from one loop (with a scalar `r` only `idiv` can overflow, and both loops fail on r = 0
  at element 0); phase 7 fuses them (§5.1).
* **L12** (Decision 37, rule 15 (j)) a `tasg` `(t1, …, tn) = c` of which some target is an L6
  store target (an `idx` with an index of kind R, A, V, M or MM, or with a `view flat` base), or
  some component has `cv` bit 2 or 4, or bit 1 with an array result: `block P m` (P the `tasg`'s
  position, which every node L12 writes takes; every site the `tasg`'s line) with (1) `tbind (L1,
  …, Ln) = c`, Li a new `.l` local of result i's type for each target that is not `skip` (a `skip`
  stays `-`), and no `cv`; (2) for each such target ti in order, `asg set ti Vi`, Vi being `lv Li`
  as it is (cv 0), under a `cvt` of `f64` (bit 1 alone), under a `dyn` (bit 2 alone) or under a
  `fix` (bit 4 alone). Bit 1 with bit 2 or 4 is one fused conversion, since the type table holds
  no `f64` array of the result's fixed shape (or no fixed-size `f64` array of the dynamic
  result's rank) to pass through: bits 1 and 2, a single `cvt` of `lv Li` whose type is the dynamic
  `f64` target type, rewritten by L7; bits 1 and 4, `xblk P TT n` (TT the fixed-size `f64` target
  type) with `tmp A = lv Li`, the `SHAPE_EXPECTED` check of L10's `fix` on A against TT's extents
  first, then value a `cvt` of `lv A` of type TT, rewritten by L7 (its fixed-size result a home,
  R9); m = 1 + the
  number of targets that are not `skip`. Each of those `asg` is then rewritten like any other (L6
  for a selection or `.flat` target, L7 for the `cvt` of an array, L10 for `dyn` and `fix`), and
  a scalar `asg` stays an `asg` (rule 2). **Every** target that is not `skip` goes through its `.l`
  local, so the stores keep the order of LANGUAGE.md §7.3 (routing only some targets would store
  those before the call's other results). The held `.l` locals are released at the block's end in
  reverse order (rule 16); a `skip` whose result holds counts is released right after the `tbind`
  (rule 15 (h)). When c is L11's `ind2sub`, step (1) is L11's statements binding I and J (the Li)
  and step (2) the same. A `tasg` that L12 does not rewrite (local, `ref` parameter, element and
  field targets with every `cv` 0 or a scalar 1) is copied unchanged and lowered as before (rule 2,
  rule 15 (j)). For §3.6.6 rule 12 the statements of the block are one statement.


**What `sealoop` rewrites in 4f** (Decisions 29, 38, 39). The rewrites L13 and L14 below implement
rules 23 (reductions) and 24 (sorting and searching) of §3.6.6; with "Lowering of the `sea.hirl`
records" they give exactly the LIR those rules give (the agreed examples of rules 23 and 24 are dump
tests, §6.2). The fixed record set cannot write that LIR as it stands (no `iand`, no type for the
64-byte accumulator home, rule 2's `mov` where rule 23 writes into the destination, no `where` value
of a counter, and no form for an `rcall`), so 4f refines the records once more (Decision 38: no
new record or field; the enumeration `wop` gains `and`):

| # | Refinement |
|---|------------|
| R12 | **Destinations of sealoop's values.** An `xblk` with a destination D (T3) hands D to its value also when (a) the value is an `ifx` (`sealower` applies (a) to every `ifx` whose parent is an `xblk`, without checking the precondition below; only the `xblk`s L13 writes, sum8's and `variance`'s values, have such a value, so the precondition holds by construction): D is the `ifx`'s R of rule 3 even when it is a local's register, with no new register and no `mov` (rule 2's exception does not apply: every operand of the rewrite, the vector and its extent, is a `tmp` evaluated before D is first written, and the arms read only the rewrite's own locals), and (b) the value is `lv L` of a scalar `.l` local that a `bind` among the `xblk`'s own statements (or in the blocks they hold) declares, an accumulator: L's register is D, as T3 makes it for a `tmp` (no `mov`). Without a destination both are lowered as before (a new register) |
| R13 | `wbin and` is the bitwise and of two `i64` operands (type 3, never a `bool`), lowered `iand d a b`; L13 writes it only for the lane `K & 7` (the `iand W K Q` of rule 23) |
| R14 | the type F8, `tfvec` of `f64` with n 8, may be appended to the type table ("Types" above); `anew P F8 0 0` is the 64-byte accumulator home of sum8 (R1: `sa P sK` of a new `slot sK 64 8`) |
| R15 | R8 is widened: an `asg set` to a scalar `.l` local declared by a `bind` may also have a scalar `lib where` value (rule 2: its `fsel`/`isel` writes the local's register: `fsel R c x R`, `isel X c K X`) |
| R16 | R10 is narrowed: a `lib sort` or `lib argsort` stays in `sea.hirl`, with two children, a dynamic vector of `f64`, `i64` or `str` elements (any expression, already rewritten: a materialized view, a selection, an L7 result, an L10 `dyn`) and the `bool` `desc`, and `sealower` lowers it by rule 24 (`rcall`); its owned first child is released right after the `rcall` (rule 15 (b)) |

*Notation* (with that of 4e). P is the position of the `lib` node; every node a rewrite writes takes P,
every site is P's line, and the nodes of the program it keeps (the operand, the `desc` value) keep
their own. V is the `tmp` of the vector operand (of a fixed-size one its home, R9), N = `tmp N =
ext(V, 0)` its length (`li` of a fixed-size extent), E its element type, s its element size. sum8
and the reduction rules below write their statements in the order listed; "the vector rule" of a
function is its rewrite with its `tmp V`, `tmp N` and `tmp D = data(V)` taken from the enclosing
`dim:` form.

* **sum8(X)** stands for the statement `tmp Z = ci 0` followed by the value

  `ifx P f64 (bin gt (lv N) (lv Z)) (xblk P f64 n { S }) (cf #0000000000000000)`

  with the statements S, in this order: `tmp H = anew P F8 0 0` (R14); `tmp A = adat P ^f64 (lv H)`
  (R2: no instruction); `tmp M = cf #8000000000000000`; `est P 8 0 (lv M) (lv A) (ci k)` for k = 0 …
  7 (R3: `stf M A - 0 8k`); `tmp D = data(V)`; `tmp Q = ci 7`; `tmp O = ci 1`; `tmp L = wbin sub (lv
  N) (lv O)`; `hloop K (lv Z) (lv L) (lv O)` with the block { `tmp W = wbin and (lv K) (lv Q)` (R13);
  `bind G = eld P f64 8 0 (lv A) (lv W)`; the statements of X(K), whose value is the element value
  `tmp Y`; `asg set (lv G) (bin add (lv G) (lv Y))` (R8: `fadd G G Y`); `est P 8 0 (lv G) (lv A) (lv
  W)` }; `tmp A0` … `tmp A7` = `eld P f64 8 0 (lv A) (ci k)` in k order; `tmp T1 = bin add (lv A0)
  (lv A1)`, `tmp T2 = bin add (lv A2) (lv A3)`, `tmp T3 = bin add (lv T1) (lv T2)`, `tmp T4 = bin
  add (lv A4) (lv A5)`, `tmp T5 = bin add (lv A6) (lv A7)`, `tmp T6 = bin add (lv T4) (lv T5)`; and
  the value `bin add P f64 (lv T3) (lv T6)`. X(K) for `sum` is `tmp Y = eld P f64 8 0 (lv D) (lv
  K)`. The `ifx` takes the destination by R12 (a) when the sum8 is an `xblk`'s value, and a new
  register otherwise (`tmp S = ` sum8's value: T1, rule 3).
* **isum** (an `i64` vector) stands for `bind R = ci 0`, `tmp D = data(V)`, then N (if not yet
  loaded: rule 23's "`li R 0`, data, loop(n; K)"), loop(N; K) { `tmp Y = eld P i64 8 0 (lv D) (lv
  K)`; `asg set (lv R) (bin add (lv R) (lv Y))` } (rule 1: `iaddc R R Y` with P's line as site:
  `integer overflow`).

* **L13** (rule 23, LANGUAGE.md §10.5) a `lib` of a reduction with one vector argument v, of type T:
  `xblk P T n` with `tmp V = v`, and then:
  * `sum` (`f64`): `tmp N`, sum8 with X(K) above; the value is sum8's `ifx`. (`i64`): isum; value
    `lv R` (R12 (b)).
  * `mean` (`f64`): `tmp N`, sum8 with `sum`'s X into `tmp S`, `tmp F = cvt P f64 (lv N)`, value

    N)`, value `bin div P f64 (lv S) (lv F)` (the sum is converted first, then n: rule 23's "an `i64`
    sum `itof` too").
  * `variance`: `tmp N`; `tmp Z0 = ci 0`; value `ifx P f64 (bin eq (lv N) (lv Z0)) (cf

    (lv N1); value bin div P f64 (lv S2) (lv F1) }) })`, where MEAN is the mean above into `tmp Mn`
    (`f64`: sum8 with `sum`'s X into `tmp S1`, `tmp F0 = cvt P f64 (lv N)`, `tmp Mn = bin div (lv
    S1) (lv F0)`; `i64`: isum without its N, `tmp S1 = cvt P f64 (lv R)`, `tmp F0 = cvt P f64 (lv
    N)`, `tmp Mn = bin div (lv S1) (lv F0)`), and DEV is sum8 into `tmp S2` with X(K) = (`f64`)

  * `std`: `tmp Vr = ` the `xblk` of `variance(v)` (with this `tmp V`), value `lib sqrt P f64 (lv

  * `max`, `min`, `argmax`, `argmin` (cmp = `gt` for `max` and `argmax`, `lt` for the others): `tmp
    N`, `tmp Z = ci 0`, `tmp Em = bin eq (lv N) (lv Z)`, `tmp Sn = cs P 5 <name>` (type 5, `str`) (the function's
    name: rule 38's `str` record, one per occurrence), `chk P EMPTY_REDUCE 1 (lv Em) (lv Sn)`, `bind R
    = cf #7FF8000000000000` (`i64`: `ci 0`), `bind Hv = cb 0`, `bind X = ci 0`, `tmp D = data(V)`,
    loop(N; K) { `tmp Y = eld P E s 0 (lv D) (lv K)`; for `f64` `tmp U = lib isnan P bool (lv Y)`,
    `tmp Kn = un not (lv U)`, `tmp G = bin cmp (lv Y) (lv R)`, `tmp Hn = un not (lv Hv)`, `tmp Tt =
    bin bor (lv Hn) (lv G)`, `tmp C = bin band (lv Kn) (lv Tt)`; for `i64` `tmp G = bin cmp (lv Y)
    (lv R)`, `tmp Hn = un not (lv Hv)`, `tmp C = bin bor (lv Hn) (lv G)`; then `asg set (lv R) (lib
    where (lv C) (lv Y) (lv R))`, `asg set (lv X) (lib where (lv C) (lv K) (lv X))` (R15), `asg set
    (lv Hv) (bin bor (lv Hv) (lv C))` }; value `lv R` (`max`, `min`) or `lv X` (`argmax`, `argmin`),
    R12 (b).
  * `nnz`, `any`, `all` (a `bool` vector): `bind R = ci 0` (`nnz`), `cb 0` (`any`) or `cb 1` (`all`),
    `tmp D = data(V)`, `tmp N`, loop(N; K) { `tmp B = eld P bool 1 0 (lv D) (lv K)`; `asg set (lv R)`
    `(wbin add (lv R) (lv B))` (`nnz`, R7: `iadd`), `(bin bor (lv R) (lv B))` (`any`) or `(bin band
    (lv R) (lv B))` (`all`) }; value `lv R` (R12 (b)). An empty vector gives 0, `false`, `true`.

  **The `dim:` forms** (a `lib name.dim` with the matrix a, element type E, and the `ci` d; result type
  T, its element size s′): `xblk P T n` with `tmp Am = a`, `tmp Rr = ext(Am, 0)`, `tmp Cc = ext(Am,
  1)`, `tmp RES = anew P T 0 1 (lv Cc)` (d = 0) or `(lv Rr)` (d = 1) (a fixed-size T: `anew P T 0 0`,
  R1), `tmp DR = data(RES)`, `tmp D = data(Am)`; then for d = 0 loop(Cc; J) { `tmp Y = ` the vector
  rule with n = Rr, data D, its loop induction I and its element index `lin(I, J, Rr)`; `est P s′ 0
  (lv Y) (lv DR) (lv J)` } and for d = 1 loop(Rr; I) { the same with n = Cc, induction J, element
  index `lin(I, J, Rr)`, the lane `wbin and (lv J) (lv Q)`, stored at I }; value `lv RES`. Inside, the
  vector rule is the `xblk` of the function above without its `tmp V`, `tmp N` and `tmp D` (they are
  Am, the extent and D of the `dim:` form, loaded once before the outer loop: a reading of rule 23,
  which has no agreed `dim:` example, its "arrnew of the result, data" taken as the data of the
  result and of the matrix, each loaded once); its value takes `tmp
  Y`'s register (T1, R12). So one sum8 home slot serves every element of the result (its `sa` runs
  in each iteration), a `max.dim`/`min.dim` checks `EMPTY_REDUCE` in each iteration of the outer loop
  (an error only when the outer extent is not 0 and the reduced one is), and the element address is
  computed in the innermost body in the post-order of its `eld` (the lead decision of 4e). Sites: P's
  line.
* **L14** (rule 24, LANGUAGE.md §10.6):
  * `sort(v, desc)`, `argsort(v, desc)`: copied as `lib` (R16); its first child is whatever the
    rewrites of its subtree made of v (a fixed-size v arrives as the `dyn` pass 2a wrote, §3.5.5,
    rewritten by L10; `.flat` by L10; a selection by L5), its second the `desc` value or the `cb 0`
    of pass 2a.
  * `find(m)`: `xblk P i64[] n` with `tmp M = m`, `tmp X = ext(M, 0)`, `bind C = ci 0`, `tmp DM =
    data(M)`, loop(X; K) { `asg set (lv C) (wbin add (lv C) (eld P bool 1 0 (lv DM) (lv K)))` } (rule
    20 (3)'s count), `tmp RES = anew P i64[] 0 1 (lv C)`, `tmp DR = data(RES)`, `tmp DM2 = data(M)`
    (rule 24: "data of the result and of m"), `bind O = ci 0`, `tmp One = ci 1`, loop(X; K2) { `tmp B =
    eld P bool 1 0 (lv DM2) (lv K2)`; `if (lv B)` { `est P 8 0 (lv K2) (lv DR) (lv O)`; O += `lv One`
    } }; value `lv RES`.
  * `find_first(m)`: `xblk P i64 n` with `tmp M = m`, `tmp X = ext(M, 0)`, `bind R = ci -1`, `tmp U = ci -1`, `tmp D =
    data(M)`, loop(X; K) { `tmp B = eld P bool 1 0 (lv D) (lv K)`; `tmp Uq = bin eq (lv R) (lv U)`;
    `tmp C = bin band (lv B) (lv Uq)`; `asg set (lv R) (lib where (lv C) (lv K) (lv R))` }; value `lv
    R`. `find_last(m)`: `xblk P i64 n` with `tmp M = m`, `tmp X`, `bind R = ci -1`, `tmp D`, loop(X; K) { `tmp B = eld …`;
    `asg set (lv R) (lib where (lv B) (lv K) (lv R))` }; value `lv R`.

So no `lib` of `sum mean variance std max min argmax argmin nnz any all find find_first find_last`,
and no `name.dim`, occurs in `sea.hirl`.

**Lead decisions of 4f** (within Decisions 38–39): the data of a `dim:` form's matrix is loaded once
before the outer loop, and the vector rule inside does not load it again; the extent of isum and of
`nnz any all` is loaded after the data, right before its loop (rule 23's order "`li R 0`, data,
loop(n; K)"); the `i64` mean converts the sum before n; operands that are views or selections are
materialized by L5 or L10 before the reduction (no `.flat` folding before phase 7's fusion, §5.1).

**What `sealoop` rewrites in 4g** (Decisions 29, 44, 45, 47, 48). The rewrites L15 (rule 29,
projection), L16 (rule 33, `match`) and L17 (rules 19, 27 (d), (f) and 15 (i): every store of a
reference or aggregate value and every store through a field path), and the extensions of L2–L14
to `str`, struct and record elements below, implement rules 26 (`str` and struct literals), 29, 30
(`str` and struct elements) and 33 of §3.6.6 and the stores of rules 19 and 27; with "Lowering of
the `sea.hirl` records" they give exactly the LIR those rules give, except that the `retain` of a borrowed value that L17
stores comes right before the store rather than right after the value (R17 (a)) (the agreed
examples of rules 26, 29, 30 (the first) and 33 come out byte for byte through `sealoop` and are dump tests, §6.2; those
of rules 15, 18 (the second), 27, 32 and 35 are `sealower`'s alone, no rewrite touching them).
`sealower` keeps rules 15, 16 and 31 for every type, rule 27 (homes, (a)–(l), except (i) and (j) and
the stores L17 takes), the reads of rule 18 (scalar indices, `fld` folding, whole struct elements),
rules 32, 34 and 35, and the `lib` calls `str`, `lower`, `error` and `args`, which stay `lib` nodes
in `sea.hirl` (R10 does not concern them: they have no array operand). The fixed record set cannot
write the rest as it stands (a replacing store of a reference element, the address of a struct
element, a struct copied into an element, the retains after a copy of reference elements, struct
homes, a field loaded through an element's address, an owned `match` scrutinee on an exit, the
copy on write of an array field, the moves of rule 15 (j) through L12's locals), so 4g refines the
records once more (Decision 44: no new record kind or field, `passes.txt` unchanged). "Holds counts"
is rule 16's: a `str`, a dynamic array, a handle, or a struct, record or fixed-size type with such
a field or element. An address is **fresh** when it is `lv D` of a `tmp D = adat (lv A)` whose `tmp A =
anew …` lies in the same `xblk` or `block` (the buffer of a new array or home, never read before).

| # | Refinement |
|---|------------|
| R17 | **Replacing stores and moved values.** (a) An `est` of a reference value (`str`, dynamic array, handle) into an address that is not fresh is a replacing store: the value V owned by rule 15 (a) (retained first when borrowed), then `ldp O D X sc off`, `stp V D X sc off`, `release O` (rules 19 (5), 27 (f), 15 (i)); the `retain` of a borrowed V is written at the `est`, right before its `ldp O`, so in an L17 block after the indices, the checks and the cows (rule 15 (a)'s "right after its own instructions" is met as "before the store" for these stores; no agreed example shows the difference, and the counts are the same at every point a program can observe); into a fresh address it stays R5's initializing store. A numeric `est` is unchanged. (b) An `est` that stands directly in a `block` (not inside a loop or `if` of it) and whose value is `lv` of an owned `tmp` written directly in the same block moves that value: no `retain`, and R11 does not release that `tmp` (it is not read after the store); only L17 and L6's single `.flat` store write this form. Everywhere else the `lv` of a `tmp` is borrowed (T1): each store retains it, and an owned `tmp` is released once by T2 or R11 (rule 17's `filled`, L6's scalar value stored into every selected element) |
| R18 | **Aggregate element addresses.** An `eld` whose `ty` is a struct, record or fixed-size array type loads nothing: its value is the element's address, a borrowed home inside the array (rules 18, 30): `li S sc`, `imul T X S`, `padd R D T`; with a `ci` index k (R3): `li O off+k·sc`, `padd R D O` (rule 26 (b)). Its address child is a `tptr` of that type, sc its size by §4.8's layout rule (`layout`, §2.6.3), off 0 |
| R19 | **Aggregate stores.** An `est` of a struct, record or fixed-size value V. Its fields sc and off are those of every `est`: sc the stride of the containing elements (the size of the array's element type, or of the home's type) and off the offset of the target inside that element (0 for a whole element, the field's offset for a field, R24: `dims[i].lim = Lim { lo: 0.0, hi: 1.0 }` has sc the size of `Dim` and off that of `lim`); the size of V's type is only the copy length N. First the target address E: with an index X, `li S sc`, `imul T X S`, `padd E D T`, followed when off ≠ 0 by `li O off`, `padd E E O` (rule 31's field address); with a `ci` index k, `li O off+k·sc`, `padd E D O` (a field of a home: k = 0). Then, only into a fresh address, a V that is a `slit` (or a `seq` whose value is one, rule 5) has its fields written in place at E (rules 26 (b), 27 (g)), and only where the `slit` is the value of an `est`, a `bind` or a `ret`: a `slit` nested as a field of another `slit` is computed into its own temporary home and copied into that field by copy(E ← V) below, never written in place; into an address that is not fresh a `slit` is first its own temporary home (L17's `tmp Vv`, rule 27 (d): "never H directly") and is stored by the copy form below, so the old reference fields are released; into a fresh address otherwise copy(E ← V) of rule 27 (c): `li N size`, `mcopy E V N`, then, when V is borrowed, `ldp R E - 0 o` and `retain R` for each reference offset o in ascending order (an owned V is moved: no retains, and its home is not released); into an address that is not fresh rule 27 (d): V's retains when V is borrowed, then E's old reference values released (`ldp O E - 0 o`, `release O`, ascending), then `li N size`, `mcopy E V N` (an owned V moved as in R17 (b)). Rule 17's struct `filled` is this copy in a loop (`li S size`, `imul T K S`, `padd E D T`, `li N size`, `mcopy E V N`, the retains) |
| R20 | **Counted copies.** An `mcpy` whose destination is a `tptr` of an element type that holds counts has as its third child the *element count* n, not the byte count: a `ci` n (a static count, written by the rewrite as the `ci` child itself, not through a `tmp`), which `sealower` writes as one `li B n·size`, or a type-3 expression, written `li S size`, `imul B N S` (the instructions the byte count of the numeric forms gives); then `mcopy D S B`; then the retains of the copied reference values on the destination: for a `ci` n unrolled, `ldp R D - 0 o` and `retain R` for each reference offset o of the n elements in ascending order (o = k·size + o′); otherwise loop(n; K) { for each reference offset o′ of the element, ascending: `ldp R D K size o′`, `retain R` } (rule 28's "the retains of `str` elements" and rule 27 (c), (i), (j), spelled here). There are no retains when the source is an owned fixed-size, struct or record home named by a `tmp` of the same `xblk`: it is moved, and T2 does not release it (rule 27 (c), (i)). An owned dynamic source (rule 27 (j)'s A, a materialized view's operand) is retained-from and released as before |
| R21 | **Struct and record homes.** R1, R2, R8 and R9 hold for struct and record types exactly as for fixed-size array types: `anew P S 0 0` is a home slot of the size of S rounded up to a multiple of 8, at least 8 (an empty struct too, lead decision L-h; rule 27 (a)); `adat` of a struct or record value is its home address (no instruction; type the `tptr` of S); a `tmp` of such a value names its home; T3 does not apply to an `xblk` of such a type. A home that holds counts is released by rule 15 (g) when it is an owned temporary (T2, R11) and by rule 16 when it is a local's. `anew` of an array of `str`, struct or record elements is rule 17's arrnew with `sea_arr_new` (ek 4) or `sea_arr_new_s` (`la` of the element type's `slay`, rule 38) whatever z: both clear the buffer (§4.8), so no reference element of a new array is ever left with undefined bits (lead decision L-j) |
| R22 | **Owned temporaries of a block on its exits.** An owned `tmp` written directly in a `block` that `sealoop` writes (R11) is also released, as a hidden local of rule 16 (f), by every `break`, `cont` and `ret` that leaves that block (rule 16 (b), (c)), innermost first with the other hidden locals: L16's S0 is released when its block is left, after the bound locals of the blocks inside it that the exit leaves (an arm's block) and before those of the blocks outside it. Only L16's scrutinee can meet an exit (L6 and L17 blocks hold no exit, and L4's held vector is a `bind`), so no earlier output changes |
| R23 | **Field paths in copy on write.** A `cow` whose child is a `fld` chain naming an array field, over the `lv` of a struct or record local, of a `ref` struct or record parameter, or of a `tmp` naming an element address (R18), is the memory form of cow (rule 19) at that field's address H and offset off (`ldp A H - 0 off`, `ldi C A - 0 0`, `li O 1`, `icmp ne S C O`, `if B S`, `rcall sea_arr_unique site 1 N 1 A`, `stp N H - 0 off`, `mov A N`, `endif B`). `ext` and `adat` of such a `fld` read the field afresh (`ldp`), except that an `adat` of the same chain in the statement right after its `cow` uses that cow's A (rule 19 (5): "data of the innermost array as (4) left it"); and, from 4g-2 (lead decision L-n), an `adat` of the `lv` of a `ref` parameter in the statement right after the `cow` of that `lv` (the address child of an `est`, or L17 step 5's `tmp D′`) uses that cow's A too (only L17 writes it; L6 reads a `ref` parameter afresh, as 4e has it); the reuse is limited to these two forms in that next statement, and every other `adat` or `ext` of that `lv` reads P afresh; in 4g-1 that `adat` reads P afresh (`ldp` after the cow), which gives the same values |
| R24 | **Fields through an element or home address.** An `eld` or `est` whose address child is a `tptr` of a struct or record type S (the data of an array of S, or `adat` of a home, R21) may load or store a field of type F at sc = the size of S and off = the field's offset in S (a nested field: the sum of the offsets along the path): rule 29's `ld? x DV K s off`, rule 18's one load `ld? R D X size off`, rule 19 (5)'s one store, rule 27 (f)'s `st? V P - 0 off` (with a `ci` index, R3). A field of a reference type is stored by R17, of a struct, record or fixed-size type by R19 (at the field's address) |
| R25 | **Moves out of L12's locals.** In an L12 block, a store `asg set ti (lv Li)` of a `.l` local Li whose type holds counts, with the value exactly `lv Li` (cv 0) and a target that L6 does not rewrite (a local, a `ref` parameter, an element by scalar indices, a field path: rule 15 (d), R17, R19), moves Li's value (rule 15 (j): "each target stored with that owned value"): no `retain`, and rule 16 does not release Li at the block's end. For a target that L17 rewrites (an element by scalar indices, a field path: `(names[i], k) = two()`), and only when Li's type holds counts (else L17 step 1 takes its `tmp Vv` as usual and nothing is moved), `sealower` sees L17's block in place of that `asg`, directly in the L12 block, with no `tmp Vv` and the block's one `est` storing `lv Li` itself (L17 step 1's exception); that store (R17's `stp`, R19's copy) moves Li: no `retain`, no retains of V's reference fields, no release of a replaced value other than the target's old one, and Li is dropped from rule 16's releases at the L12 block's end. `sealower` recognizes the form by that operand, which no other rewrite writes: an `est` whose value is `lv Li` of a `.l` local of the `tbind` that begins the L12 block (R8), in a `block` that stands directly in that L12 block; L6 always binds its value first (`tmp Vv`, `bind Vv`, step 1) and stores `lv Vv` or an element of DV, so an L6 block (a target with a selection or a `view flat` base, also `(names[0..3], k) = two()` and `(names.flat[i], k) = …`) is never a move. Each Li is moved at most once. A target that L6 rewrites (a selection, `.flat`) and a converted component (`cvt`, `dyn`, `fix` of `lv Li`) keep Li as a held local released at the block's end, as 4e has it. (This also drops one `retain` and one `release` from the 4e-reachable form of a dynamic-array result stored into a local or `ref` parameter target of an L12 block; no golden pins that form, and only reference-count instructions change, never output.) From 6c (L-dq): an `est` whose value is `lv Li`, Li a `.l` local whose type holds no counts and that the `tbind` beginning the `est`'s own block lists (L19's element body for k ≥ 2: that `tbind`, then one `est` per kept result), is the plain `est`, with nothing to move; any other `est` of an L12 `.l` local that is not the move above stays `BAD_RECORD`. |

R5's "4g adds the replacing store" is R17. No record, field or enumeration word is added, so
`passes.txt`, `tools/seaval.bas` (generic) and the record tables of every pass are unchanged.

*Notation* (with that of 4e and 4f). P is the position of the rewritten node (the `proj`, the
`match`, the `asg` or `tasg`); every node L15–L17 write takes P and every site is P's line, while
the nodes of the program they keep keep their own: L16's `cs` patterns and arm blocks, the operands
and values (lead decision L-l). s(S) is the size of a struct, record or fixed-size type S and
off(S, f) the offset of its field f (of a nested field, the sum along the path), both from §4.8's
layout rule through the module `layout` (§2.6.3); the reference offsets of a type are rule 15 (g)'s
list, ascending.

* **L15** (rule 29, LANGUAGE.md §4.7) `proj i` of a vector V of structs or records (element S, field
  f of type F, F's element size sF): `xblk P F[] n` with `tmp V = v`; `tmp N = ext(V, 0)`; `tmp R =
  anew P F[] 0 1 (lv N)`; `tmp DR = data(R)`; `tmp DV = data(V)`; loop(N; K) { `est P sF 0 (eld P F
  s(S) off(S, f) (lv DV) (lv K)) (lv DR) (lv K)` } (R24; a `str` field's borrowed `ldp` is retained
  by the initializing `est`, R5); value `lv R`. Lowered, this is rule 29's example exactly: `ldi i2`
  (N; `tmp V` is T1's alias of `p1`), arrnew `li i3 1`, `li i4 1`, `li i5 1`, `rcall sea_arr_new_u`
  (an `f64` field: z = 0 gives the unclearing entry, rule 17), `ldp p7 p6` (DR), `ldp p8 p1` (DV), loop(N; K),
  `ldf f14 p8 i13 48 8`, `stf f14 p7 i13 8 0`. A fixed-size `S[n]` base: `ext` is its `li`, `adat` its
  home (R2, R21); the result is always the dynamic `F[]` (LANGUAGE.md §4.7). A `str` field gives a
  `str[]` (`sea_arr_new`, R21). A base that is a view or a selection (`dims[0..2].nom`,
  `(A.flat).name`) is materialized first by L5 or L10, then projected (lead decision L-e: no fusion
  before phase 7, §5.1).
* **L16** (rule 33, LANGUAGE.md §7.6) `match S a1 … an` (`seacheck` has checked that the last arm is `_`
  and no arm follows it): `block P 2` { `tmp S0 = S`; C(1) }, where for a pattern arm i with patterns
  p1 … pk, C(i) is `if P 1` with the condition cond_i, the arm's block, and as its `else` part C(i + 1),
  or for the `_` arm its block; cond_i is `bin eq P bool (lv S0) (cs p1)` for k = 1, and for k ≥ 2
  `xblk P bool k` with the statements `tmp Qj = bin eq P bool (lv S0) (cs pj)` for j = 1 … k and the
  value `bin bor P bool (… (bin bor (lv Q1) (lv Q2)) …) (lv Qk)`. A `match` with only the `_` arm is
  `block P 2` { `tmp S0 = S`; that arm's block }. Checked by hand against rule 33's example: `tmp S0 =
  lv a` is T1's alias of `p1`; `la p3 d1`, `rcall sea_str_cmp - 1 i4 2 p1 p3`, `li i5 0`, `icmp eq
  i6` (Q1's register), the same for `"y"` (`p7`, `i8`, `i9`, `i10`), `ior i11 i6 i10`, `if 1 i11`,
  `li i2 1`, `else 1`, `li i2 2`, `endif 1`: identical. An owned scrutinee (a call, `args()[0]` by rule
  15 (f)) is a temporary of the block, released after the last `endif` (R11) and by every exit
  through the `match` (R22): rule 16 (f)'s hidden local.
* **L17** (rules 19, 27 (d), (f), 15 (i)) an `asg` (any op) whose target (a) is a field path, that is
  holds a `fld` (`s.f`, `s.a.b`, `s.v[k]`, `dims[d].nom`, `a[i].v[k]`), or (b) is an element by scalar
  indices whose element type holds counts or is a struct or record (`names[i]`, `dims[i]`, an element
  of a `str[n]` or `S[n]`); a target with a selection or a `view flat` base is L6's (with a field root,
  below), and the assignment of a whole local or `ref` parameter stays an `asg` for `sealower`
  (rule 15 (d), rule 27 (d), rule 31). It becomes `block P n` with, for op `set`:
  1. the value: `tmp Vv = value` (a `slit` an owned temporary home, R21); except that in an L12
     block, a value that is exactly `lv Li` (cv 0) of one of that block's `.l` locals whose type
     holds counts writes no statement here, and step 6's `est` has the value `lv Li` itself in
     place of `lv Vv` (the hidden local cannot change before the store; R25 moves it);
  2. for a root that is a `ref` parameter of a dynamic array type, `tmp B = lv T` (rule 19: `ldp B P - 0 0`
     after the value, before the indices); a local root needs none (its `lv` is its register);
  3. the path's scalar indices, left to right in source order (`tmp Ik`), up to the first `idx`
     under a field of an array element one of whose indices holds a `$`;
  4. the checks, outermost array first, against the arrays as they are: `tmp Xk = ext(Bk, d)` and
     `chkb d (lv Ik) (lv Xk)` per dimension, the linear position of a matrix as `lin` of rule 18; the
     next array through a field of an element: `tmp Dk = data(Bk)`, `tmp Ek = eld P S s(S) 0 (lv Dk)
     (lv Ik)` (R18, the element's address), `tmp Bk+1 = fld (lv Ek) j` (`ldp V E - 0 off`, rule 27
     (e)); through a field of a struct local or `ref` parameter `tmp Bk+1 = fld (lv s) j`. From the
     `idx` at which step 3 stopped on, each `idx`'s indices are evaluated here, right after its
     `tmp Bk` and before its checks, a `$` among them being `ext(Bk, d)` of that level's array (read
     before any cow; a cow changes no extent), so evaluation stays left to right and
     `a[5].v[$ - 1] = 1.0` on a 5-element `a` reports `a`'s index 5 first (LANGUAGE.md §5.5);
  5. copy on write, outermost first (rule 19 (4)), each array taken as the cow before it left it
     (R23: the cow's register A, rule 19's "the array is then A", for a `ref` parameter also the
     array the memory form stored; for a `ref` parameter root from 4g-2, lead decision L-n, in 4g-1
     read from P afresh after the cow), never step 4's `Dk` or `Bk` (loaded before any cow). For a
     dynamic root array T (a local or a `ref` parameter): `cow (lv T)`, and, when the path goes on
     through a field of its element, `tmp D′ = adat (lv T)` right after that cow (A), `tmp E′ = eld P
     S s(S) 0 (lv D′) (lv I0)`, the first field level's array being `fld (lv E′) j`; for a struct
     root (a struct local or `ref` parameter s) there is no root array and the first field level's
     array is `fld (lv s) j`. Then, for each field level outermost first, F its array (as just
     given, or the previous level's `fld (lv E′) j′`): `cow F` when F is of a dynamic array type,
     and, when the path goes on through a field of F's element, `tmp D′ = adat F` right after that
     cow (A), `tmp E′ = eld P S′ s(S′) 0 (lv D′) (lv I)` with I the index of F on the path, the
     next level's array being `fld (lv E′) j′`. So `s.items[i].v[k] = x` writes `cow (fld (lv s)
     items)`, `tmp D′ = adat (fld (lv s) items)`, `tmp E′ = eld P S′ s(S′) 0 (lv D′) (lv I0)`, `cow
     (fld (lv E′) v)`; and `a[0].w[0].v[0] = 9.0` after `let b = a` copies `a`, then the `w` of
     `a`'s copy, then that `w`'s element's `v`, and `b` keeps every old value. A fixed-size array or
     a field in a home needs none;
  6. the store, one `est` right after the last `cow` (or the checks): `est sc off (lv Vv) A X` with
     A = `adat` of the innermost array (R23's reuse of the cow's register; of a `ref` parameter
     root from 4g-2, in 4g-1 read afresh, L-n) or of the home (`adat (lv
     s)`, R21), X its linear position (`lv I`, `lin(I0, I1, X0)`, or `ci 0` for a field of a home),
     sc and off the element size and offset or, for a field, R24's s(S) and off(S, f): R17 for a
     reference value, R19 for an aggregate, the plain store for a number (`stf V D X 48 8` for
     `dims[d].nom = x`, `stf V P - 0 off` for `s.x = v`). Vv is moved by R17 (b) or R19; an `lv Li` value by R25.

  For op ≠ `set` (rule 19's compound form, rule 15 (i)): step 3; `tmp R0 = xblk P T 2` { `tmp T0 = `
  the read of the target (its own `idx` and `fld` expression with each index replaced by its `lv
  Ik`), lowered by `sealower`'s rules 18 and 27 (e) with its own base load and checks; `tmp Vv = value`; value `bin op P T (lv T0) (lv Vv)` (rule 1 or
  rule 32, the `asg`'s line) }, so T2 releases an owned Vv and a retained read right after the
  operation; then steps 2, 4, 5 and 6 storing `lv R0` (the base loaded again and the checks repeated:
  the value may have changed the arrays through a `ref` argument). Sites: the `asg`'s line. For rule
  12 the block is one statement. So no `fld` reaches `sealower` in an assignment target, and
  `sealower` writes no store of a reference or aggregate element or field of its own (its rule-19
  code stays the numeric one of 4d).

*The 4e and 4f rewrites over `str`, struct and record elements* (extensions; no new numbers; the
sub-step of Decision 47 that brings each in brackets):

| Rewrite | 4g extension |
|---------|--------------|
| L2 `filled` | [4g-1] E `str`: `est 8 0 (lv V) (lv D) (lv K)`, V the `tmp` of the value: borrowed (T1), so `retain V` before each `stp`; an owned V is released once by T2, after `endif` (rule 17). [4g-2] E a struct or record: `est s(E) 0 (lv V) (lv D) (lv K)` by R19, a copy with retains into each element |
| L3 `len` | [4g-1] of a `str`: `ext P 3 0` |
| L4 `fore` | [4g-1] X = `eld P str 8 0` (a borrowed `ldp`, rule 30's first example exactly). [4g-2] X = `eld P S s(S) 0` (R18, the element's address); a fixed-size `str[n]` or `S[n]` vector is bound by copy into H's home with the retains of a borrowed source (rule 27 (b), (c)) and released at the block's end (rule 16): rule 30 (1)–(3) |
| L5 selections | [4g-1] the result's stores are initializing: a `str` element read borrowed and retained (R5). [4g-2] struct and record elements copied by R19 from the R18 address; the projection of a selection by L15 after L5 (L-e) |
| L6 selection stores | [4g-1] the stores into a `str` target are replacing (R17); a scalar `str` value is retained at each store and an owned one released at the block's end (R11), an array value read borrowed and retained; the single `.flat` store with a scalar index moves an owned value (R17 (b)), and its compound form computes the operation as L17's `tmp R0 = xblk …` (an owned value released right after the operation, rule 15 (i)). [4g-2] struct elements by R19; step 1's copy of a fixed-size value that is `lv` of the target's root, when its element type holds counts (`a[:] = a` with `a: str[3]`), takes R20's form: `mcpy data(Vv) data(V0) (ci n)` with n the element count, then the retains of the copied reference values (V0, the root, is borrowed), and that new home, an owned temporary of the block, is released by rule 15 (g) at the block's end (R11; R1 as amended). A target whose root path holds a `fld` (`s.v[0..2] = …`, `dims[d].v[:] = …`) interleaves L17's path steps with L6's steps in the order of rule 19 and LANGUAGE.md §5.5: the value (L6 step 1); all indices in source order, L17 step 3's path indices merged with L6 step 2's selection indices (`dims[p()].v[q()..3] = 0.0` evaluates `p()`, then `q()` and the range), except that from the first `idx` under a field of an element whose indices hold a `$` (`dims[d].v[$-2..$] = 0.0`), that `idx`'s indices, the selection's included, are evaluated after the path's checks before it (L17 step 4), `$` being that level's `ext(Bk, d)`; all checks, L17 step 4 (the path, outermost first) then L6 step 3 (IX 2 on the field array); L6 step 4's shape check; the cows, L17 step 5 (the root, then each field level, R23) in place of L6 step 5; then L6 step 6, whose `tmp DT = adat (fld …)` stands right after the last cow and uses its register (R23), and the nest. The field array's base for IX is that `fld` read afresh at each use, as a `ref` parameter is |
| L7 element-wise | [4g-1] (Decision 45) `str` operands read `eld P str 8 0` (borrowed); F is `bin cat` (owned, moved by the initializing `est`) or a comparison (`bool`); a scalar `str` operand is its `tmp`, an owned one released after the nest (T2). [4g-2] fixed-size `str` operands and results (homes that hold counts, R21) |
| L9 literals | [4g-1] (b) `str` elements `est 8 0 e (lv D) (ci k)`, retained when borrowed (rule 26's agreed example exactly: `li i1 2`, arrnew with `li i2 4`, `rcall sea_arr_new`, `ldp p6`, `la p7 d1`, `retain p7`, `stp p7 p6 - 0 0`, …); (c) concatenation with `str` parts (each copied element retained, the parts released after the copies); (d) `[]` of `str[]` (R21). [4g-2] struct and record elements by R19 (a `slit` written in place at `li O off`, `padd E D O`; another value copied); `[]` of `S[]` |
| L10 views, `dyn`, `fix` | [4g-1] materialized `.flat`, `.col`, `.row` of a `str` array by R20 (the element count, the retain loop); `.T` element by element (an `est` of a borrowed element: retained). [4g-2] `dyn` and `fix` of `str[n]`, `S[n]` and of `str` and struct matrices by R20; the materialized views of struct and record arrays |
| L12 tuple assignment | [4g-1] also a `tasg` with a target that L17 rewrites (a `str` element), each target through its `.l` local with R25's moves. [4g-2] field-path and aggregate targets the same |
| L14 `sort`, `argsort` | [4g-1] a dynamic `str` vector (R16 as written). [4g-2] a fixed-size `str[n]` arrives as the `dyn` of pass 2a, rewritten by L10 with R20 |

So no `proj` or `match` occurs in `sea.hirl`, and no `asg` or `tasg` whose target holds a `fld`.

**Lead decisions of 4g in this section** (within Decisions 44 and 47; §0): views and selections under
a projection are materialized first (L-e); every array of `str`, struct or record elements is
allocated by a clearing entry (L-j, R21); the struct layouts come from the module `layout` (L-k);
every node L15–L17 write takes the rewritten node's position, L16 keeping its patterns' and arms'
own (L-l); an empty struct's home is an 8-byte slot and its arrays have element size 0 (L-h, R21).

**What the passes validate.** `sealoop` validates its input `sea.hir` as `sealower` did before
4e-0: every record against `passes.txt` (fields, enumeration words, positions within the file
list), the record kinds the current sub-phase implements (from 4e also `dyn`, `fix`, `view`, `all`,
`arr`, `row`, `rng` as an index or a value, and the types `tfvec`, `tfmat`; from 4f the `lib` calls of
L13 and L14 with their argument types of §2.6.2, "Readings fixed by 4f", `name.dim` only of the nine
reductions with a `ci` 0 or 1, and `sort`/`argsort` with a dynamic vector and a `bool`), and the tree
(`BAD_RECORD`, `BAD_TREE`, §2.6.2). `sealower` validates `sea.hirl` the same way, with the sets `H HF HL`, and in addition: no
`fore` and none of the rewritten `lib` calls; from 4e none of the array expressions of R10; each `tmp`
local bound by exactly one `tmp`, before every `lv` of it in node order, its type equal to the
`tmp`'s child's, and never the target of a `bind`, `tbind`, `asg`, `tasg` or `rarg`; the `l` of
an `rcnt` of type 3 and its `e` of type 2, each written only by that `rcnt` (from 4e); a `bind` of a
`.l` local only where R8 allows it (one of an array type only directly in a `block`), a `tbind` of `.l` locals only as the first
statement of a `block` (L12, R8), every `idx` with as many indices as its base's rank (a `view`
base, `.flat` with its one linear index included, never survives `sealoop`, R10), and an `asg` to a `.l` local only with op `set` and only to a scalar
local declared by a `bind` (`sealower` marks a `.l` local when a `bind` declares it and checks that
mark, not merely that the local's `loc` record is a scalar `let` `.l` local) (from 4f its value may also be a scalar `lib where`, R15); a `tmp` of a `tptr` type only of an `adat` or `cdat`; an `hloop`'s
local of mut `for` and type 3, its first three children of type 3, its last a `block`; `ext` of an
array or a `str`, dim < the array's rank (0 for a `str`); `adat` of an array, `ty` the `tptr` of its
element type; `eld` with an address of a `tptr` type whose `elt` is `ty`, an index of type 3; `est`
with an address of a `tptr` type whose `elt` is the value's type; `anew` with `ty` a dynamic array type of
rank r and children of type 3, or a fixed-size array type with r = 0 and z = 0; `wbin` `add`, `sub`
or `mul` of two operands of type 2 or 3, `wbin and` (from 4f) of two operands of type 3; from 4f a
`lib sort` or `lib argsort` with exactly two children, a dynamic vector of `f64`, `i64` or `str`
elements and a type-2 `desc`, and its result type that vector's type (`sort`) or `i64[]`
(`argsort`), R16; an appended `tfvec` only of `f64` with n 8, and rejected as a duplicate when an earlier type
of the table is already `f64[8]` (a program that declares `f64[8]` itself has that type reused by
`sealoop`, so its file appends none; R14); `chkb` of two type-3 children; `chk` with a type-2 condition and `err` a
run-time error of `errors.inc` whose arguments take n slots; `rcnt` of three type-3 children;
`cow` of an `lv` of a local or `ref` parameter of a dynamic array type; `mcpy` of two addresses of a
`tptr` type and a type-3 count; `cdat` with `ty` a `tptr` whose `elt` is the type of each of its n ≥ 1
children, every child a `ci`, `cf` or `cb`; an `xblk`'s `ty` equal to its last
child's. Any violation is `BAD_RECORD` (`BAD_TREE` for the tree). `tools/seaval.bas` validates the
format `hirl` (sets `H HF HL`) with its generic checks (§2.10); it needed no change for 4f, since it
reads the enumeration `wop` (with `and`) and the types (with F8) from `passes.txt` and the file
itself.

**What the passes validate in 4g** (in addition to the above; Decision 44). `sealoop` accepts in
`sea.hir` the kinds of the current sub-step (4g-1: `cs` anywhere, `bin cat`, the comparisons and
`asg add` of `str` operands and their element-wise forms, `lib str`, `lower`, `error`, `args`,
`len` of a `str`, `match` and `arm`, the `str` element type in `tvec` and `tmat`, the `str` forms
of `filled`, `sort` and `argsort`; 4g-2 also `tstruct`, `trec` and their `fd` records, the struct
and record element types, `tfvec`/`tfmat` of `str`, struct and record elements, `slit`, `fld`,
`proj`, field targets), each against `passes.txt`, the readings of §2.6.2 ("Readings fixed by 4g")
and §3.5.7's checks; anything else of 4g stays `BAD_RECORD` until its sub-step. `sealower`
checks in addition: no `proj`, `match` or `arm`; no `fld` in the target of an `asg` or `tasg`, and
no `asg` whose target L17 rewrites (an element by scalar indices whose element type holds counts
or is a struct or record), and no `tasg` with such a target (L12 routes it, R10); an `est` of a reference value into a fresh address or, by R17, into any
other address of a `tptr` type, a moved value only in the form of R17 (b) (directly in a `block`,
`lv` of an owned `tmp` of that block that is read nowhere after the store); an `eld` or `est` of a
struct, record or fixed-size `ty` with off 0 only with an address of the `tptr` of that type (a
whole element, R18, R19), and with any other address or off only as R24's field clause below; a
`slit` value of an `est` only into a fresh address (R19); an
`eld` or `est` through the address of a struct or record S (R24) only with sc the size of S and off
the offset of a field, nested ones included, whose type is `ty` (the value's type for an `est`), as
`layout` computes them; an `mcpy` into a `tptr` whose `elt` holds counts with a type-3 element
count (R20); a `cow` of an `lv` (4e) or of a `fld` chain over R23's roots naming a field of a
dynamic array type; `adat` of an array, of a struct or record home (R21) or of such a `fld` chain;
`anew` also of a struct or record type with r = 0 and z = 0 (R21); a `tmp` directly in a `block`
only where R11 and R22 allow it; R25's moves only for an L12 block's stores of its own `.l` locals
with the value exactly `lv Li` and a target that L6 did not rewrite: an `asg set ti (lv Li)`
directly in the L12 block, or one `est` whose value is `lv Li` in a block directly in it (L17 step
1's exception: an `est` whose value is `lv Li` of a local declared by an L12 block's `tbind` is
valid only as that block's L17 store, in a block directly in it, each Li at most once; `est`s of
other `.l` locals are unchanged, and an L6 block, which stores `lv Vv`, is never a move); appended types only `tptr`
(also of struct and record types) and F8, as before. Any violation is `BAD_RECORD`. `tools/seaval.bas`
needs no change for 4g (no record, field or word is added).

**What `sealoop` rewrites in 4h** (Decisions 53 and 55; §3.6.6 rule 37, whose LIR is unchanged).
When `sea.hir` has more than one `#file` record, file 0 is the prelude and a function whose `fn`
record's `pos` is in file 0 is a prelude function (rule 37). `sealoop` reads the whole file before
it writes (as before), so it has every prelude body when it reaches a call.

* **L18** (rule 37) `call P ty fid n` with children a1 … an whose callee F is a prelude function,
  with parameters p1 … pn and k results (k 0 when F's result type is 1, m for a `ttuple` of m
  results, else 1): `xblk P ty n` whose statements are `tmp Ai = ai` for i = 1 … n in order (Ai a
  new `.l` local of pi's type; ai the argument as written, already of pi's type, since pass 2a
  made every conversion explicit, and rewritten by L1–L17 like any expression), and whose value is
  `iblk P ty k` with one child B, a copy of F's body `block` in which: (1) every node takes P (the
  copied `block`s and the `cs` patterns included); (2) every `lv` of pi refers to Ai; (3) every
  other local of F is replaced by a new `.i` local of the caller (Locals, above); (4) every `ret
  P′ m V1 … Vm` becomes `iret P m V1 … Vm`; (5) every `call` of a prelude function in the copy is
  itself rewritten by L18, so inlining is recursive (Decision 55). The whole `xblk` is then
  rewritten by L1–L17 like any code of the caller (the copy's `fore` by L4, its `zeros` by L1, its
  selection reads by L5, its element stores by L17, …). A `seq` whose value is the call keeps its
  `bind`s, its value becoming the `xblk`. When every call is rewritten, `sealoop` drops every
  prelude function (its records from `fn` to `end`) and renumbers the remaining functions densely
  in their order, rewriting every `fid` field (lead decision L-v): in 4h the fields of `fn` and
  `call` records; an `inst` record cannot reach `sealoop` before phase 6 (`seaname` rejects
  elemental functions by the phase rule, and `sealoop`'s reader rejects `inst` as `BAD_RECORD`),
  so rewriting its `fid` belongs to the phase-6 work that teaches the reader `inst`. No prelude
  function is a LIR function (rule 37), and `sealower` requires dense `fid`s. A file with no
  prelude function (every `--no-prelude` compilation, and every program that calls none of the
  four, since pass 2b drops unreached functions) is written as before; with one, the `fid`s of the
  program's functions after `.main` move down by the number of prelude functions dropped.
  Example (the stage golden `inl_half`, §6.2): the hand-written two-file `sea.hir` of rule 37's
  example (`fn half(x: f64) -> f64 { return x / 2.0 }` in file 0, `let y = half(3.0)` on line 1 of
  file 1) gives in `.main` the locals `y` (1) and `.l1` (2, the parameter's `tmp`), the argument
  `cf` at its own position, then at the call's position the `tmp` of `.l1`, the copy (`lv` of
  `.l1`, `cf` 2.0, `bin div`, `iret` with k 1, its `block`), the `iblk` (`ty` 4, k 1) and the `xblk`
  (`ty` 4, n 1), then `y`'s `bind`; `half` is dropped. Lowered as "Lowering of the `sea.hirl`
  records" says, it gives rule 37's example byte for byte.

Refinements of 4h (no record or field beyond `iblk` and `iret`; lead decision L-w: each reading
makes an inline call behave exactly as the call it replaces):

| # | Refinement |
|---|------------|
| R26 | **Inline `xblk`.** An `xblk` whose n statements are exactly one `tmp` per parameter, in order, and whose value is an `iblk` is an *inline `xblk`*. Its `ty` may be a `ttuple` (only as the child of a `tbind`, `tasg`, `tret` or `eval`, or as the value of a `seq` that is such a child, L12's `tbind` of `.l` locals included) or 1 (only under `eval`). It is owned exactly when its results are reference values, as a call is (rule 15 (k)). T1 holds for its `tmp`s: an `lv M` argument makes Ai another name for M, rule 37's "each parameter's register is its argument's register"; T2 releases its owned `tmp`s (owned argument temporaries) right after its value, in the order R27 gives (after the `mov`s of a `tbind`, before the stores of a `tasg`), as rule 15 (b) releases them after a call; T3 does not apply (its value is no `lv`): its destination is handed to the `iblk`. An `iblk` bounds every search for an enclosing node: within its body, T2's "innermost `xblk`", R11's and R22's "directly in a `block`" ("in no `xblk`") and R8's "directly in a `block`" stop at the `iblk`, so a `tmp` inside the body is never a temporary of an `xblk` outside the `iblk`, and an owned `tmp` directly in a `block` inside the body, with no `xblk` between it and the `iblk`, is R11's and R22's (released at that block's end and on the exits that leave it), whatever `xblk`s enclose the inline call. Validation: every statement of an inline `xblk` is a `tmp` and its value an `iblk` (`sealower`). For rule 12's "one statement", each statement of the inlined body is one, and an `iret` is a statement as a `ret` is (L-cz). |
| R27 | **The value of an `iblk`** (the one statement of the inline destination rule; §3.6.6 refers to it). Without a destination its value is R1 … Rk, with no `mov`: so rule 15 (d)'s new register V of an `asg set` to a reference local is R1 (`release L`, `mov L R1`, as for a call), an `asg set` to a scalar `ref` parameter stores R1 as rule 2 stores a call's result there, and under a `tmp` (the inline `xblk` as an operand, a library argument, a `fix`, a `match` scrutinee, an argument of another inline call: `linspace(…) + 1.0`, `sum(linspace(…))`) L is another name for R1, with no `mov`, as T1 makes it for an `ifx` (rule 3). With a destination D of rule 2 or 3 (a `bind`, an `asg set` to a scalar local, an operand or arm register), `mov D R1` after `enddo B` (rule 37: "a destination of rule 2 receives it with `mov`"). This takes precedence over T3: when an `xblk` with a destination D has the value `lv L` and its `tmp L` binds an inline `xblk`, T3 does not apply, and the destination receives `mov D R1`. Under a `tbind` or `tasg` each component is stored exactly as rule 2 (d) and rule 15 (j) store a call's new result register for that target (a local, a `ref` parameter, a numeric element by scalar indices; `itof` for cv 1; a `_` that holds counts released, rule 15 (h)); under a `tbind` the `mov`s into the locals come first, then T2's releases of the owned argument `tmp`s, then rule 15 (h)'s releases of the `_` components; under a `tasg` the owned argument `tmp`s are released before the stores, as after a call. Under a `tret`, the releases of rule 16 (c), then `ret k R1 … Rk`; under an `eval`, each owned Ri released right after the statement (rule 15 (h)). |
| R28 | **`.i` locals are ordinary locals.** They are declared by `bind`, `forr`, `tbind`, a `seq`'s `bind` or, for a loop variable that L4 rewrites, a `tmp`; they are assigned, indexed, compound-assigned and released (rule 16) exactly as source locals; R8's limits and `sealower`'s checks of `.l` locals do not apply to them (the prefix `.i` is not `.l`). |
| R29 | **Exits of an `iblk`.** A `break` or `cont` inside an `iblk` names a loop inside it. An `iret` releases, after its values are owned, the bound locals of every enclosing block inside the `iblk`'s body (innermost first, rule 16 (c)), the hidden locals inside it (L4's H, an owned `match` scrutinee) and the owned `tmp`s of the blocks it leaves inside it (R22), never anything of the caller. Rule 16 (a): no releases at the end of a block whose last statement is an `iret`, nor at the end of the body block of an `iblk` with k ≥ 1 (never reached: `missing return`, LANGUAGE.md §8.1); the body block of an `iblk` with k = 0 ends with its releases and `exit B` unless its last statement is an `iret` (rule 37 (4)). Rule 15 (a)'s places that need an owned value include `iret`. |
| R30 | **Rule 12 and an inline call.** The reads of an inline `xblk`'s `tmp`s are the arguments of the inlined call (rule 37 (1)), and rule 12 applies to them exactly as to a call's arguments: its scalar copy by evaluation order (`g(linspace(0.0, 1.0, n), h(ref n))` copies n into the parameter's register), and its protections (a)–(c) of reference and struct values when a later `tmp` of the same inline `xblk` holds a call whose roots include the read's root (`setdiff(v, grow(ref v))`: the first parameter is v as it was before `grow` ran). A `tmp` so protected names the protected copy (rule 12 (a)'s `mov T L` and `retain T`, (b)'s retained load, (c)'s temporary home), not M: T1's alias does not apply, and the copy is an owned `tmp` that T2 releases with the inline `xblk`'s other owned `tmp`s. Only a call after the inline `xblk` never needs them, because the `iblk` consumes its arguments before any later call of the statement (rule 12: "a value consumed before the call needs nothing"). The reads inside the body are of the copy's own locals, which no `ref` argument outside it reaches. |

**What the passes validate in 4h** (in addition to the above; Decision 53, lead decision L-x).
`sealoop`, on its input `sea.hir`: a prelude function has kind `fn` (not `elem`), no `ref`
parameter, no `tret` in its body and a result type that is 1, a scalar, `str`, a dynamic array or
a `ttuple` of those; the prelude's call graph has no cycle; a `call` of a prelude function has n
equal to its np and each child's `ty` equal to its parameter's type (pass 2a made every conversion
explicit). `sealower`, in addition to §3.5.9: an `iblk` only as the value of an inline `xblk`
(R26: every statement a `tmp`, the value an `iblk`), its one child a `block`, k consistent with `ty`; an `iret` only inside an `iblk`, its k that
of the innermost `iblk` and its values of the result types; no `ret` or `tret` inside an `iblk`; a
`break` or `cont` inside an `iblk` only within a loop inside it; an `xblk` of a `ttuple` type or of
type 1 only as R26 allows; the `fid`s dense (as before). `.i` locals need no check of their own.
Any violation is `BAD_RECORD`. `tools/seaval.bas` reads the two records from `passes.txt` and
needs no change.

**Capacity.** `sealoop` counts `sea.hirl` as a whole: all its nodes against `SEA_LIM_NODES`
(`program too large: nodes`), all its locals, the new `.l` locals included, against
`SEA_LIM_SYMBOLS` (`symbols`), and all its types, the appended `tptr` types (and from 4f the type F8, R14) included, against
`SEA_LIM_TYPES` (`types`); a limit is reported at the position of the node whose rewrite would
exceed it (status 10, §2.6.2). Only a program near a limit can see it. The symbols count is the
number of `par` and `loc` records of all the functions (counted while `sealoop` reads the file)
plus the `.l` locals the rewrites add, and it is checked only when a rewrite adds a local, so a
program without rewrites is never rejected on symbols; a program near the limit may see `program
too large: symbols` from `sealoop` at the position of the rewritten node, although `seaname`
accepted it (pass 2b keeps no running count of all the symbols with its `.j` locals and is not the
model: it checks only its own `.j` locals, program-wide, against `SEA_LIM_SYMBOLS`, a guard for its
internal table, L-eb). From 4h
the nodes L18 adds (the copies, the `tmp`s, the `xblk` and the `iblk`) count against
`SEA_LIM_NODES` and its `.l` and `.i` locals against `SEA_LIM_SYMBOLS`, a limit reported at the
position of the `call` being inlined.

v { } … }`, whose `fore` is at 0:3:5. In `sea.hirl` the type table gains `tptr 11 4` after `tvec 10
4`, and the function begins (locals: `v` 1, `x` 2, `.l1` … `.l7` 3 … 9):

(then the `printf` statement and the body block as in `sea.hir`). Lowered by §3.6.6 it is rule
30's example exactly: `mov p2 p1`, `retain p2` (the `bind`), `ldi i3 p2 - 0 16` (`.l2`), `li i4
0`, `icmp gt i5 i3 i4`, `if 1 i5`, `ldp p6 p2 - 0 40`, `li i7 1`, `isub i8 i3 i7`, `loop 2 i9 i4 i8
i7`, `ldf f10 p6 i9 8 0` (into `x`), `endloop 2`, `endif 1`, `release p2` (the end of the block).

### 3.6 `sea.lir1` and `sea.lir`

LIR (§2.4) is a linear, typed three-address code. The body of a LIR file is the **functions**,
then the **data records** (after the functions, so that pass 3a can write each function as soon
as it is lowered and the data it collected at the end, §2.7).

#### 3.6.1 Registers and values

A virtual register is written as a class letter and a number: `i` (`i64`), `f` (`f64`), `p`
(`ptr`, an address), `x` (`v2f64`), `y` (`v4f64`), `m` (a lane mask). Numbers are unique within a
function across all classes and given from 1 in order of first appearance in the function's
records (record order, fields left to right; the parameters, in the `func` record, come first).
A register is a variable: several instructions may write it (LIR is not in SSA form), and it is
local to its function. A mask has the lane count (2 or 4) of the instruction that defines it and
is used only with vectors of that lane count.

Sea values in registers: `i64` and `bool` (0 or 1) in `i`; `f64` in `f`; `str` values, dynamic
arrays and handles as `p` (the address of the runtime object, layouts in `rt.inc`, §4.8). Structs
and fixed-size arrays live in memory (stack slots, or inside arrays and structs) and are
addressed with `p` registers; pass 3b scalar-replaces them into registers where §5.3 allows.

#### 3.6.2 Data records

| Record | Fields | Meaning |
|--------|--------|---------|
| `str` | `lab v:s` | a static, never-freed string object with the bytes v |
| `fmt` | `lab k:u`, then k `ftext`/`fconv` records | a pre-parsed format (LANGUAGE.md §11.1) |
| `ftext` | `v:s` | literal bytes |
| `fconv` | `fl:fl w:u? p:u? conv:conv cls:rcls` | a conversion and the register class of its argument (`i`, `f`; `p` for `%s`) |
| `dat` | `lab elt:delt n:u`, then n `dvi` (elt `i64`, `bool`) or `dvf` (elt `f64`) records | a read-only element buffer (constant array data) |
| `dvi` | `v:i` | one `i64` or `bool` element |
| `dvf` | `v:f` | one `f64` element |
| `slay` | `lab size:u n:u`, then n `soff` records | the layout descriptor of a struct type that is the element type of a dynamic array (§4.8 `SEA_SL_*`): its size in bytes and its n reference fields (phase 4) |
| `soff` | `v:u` | the byte offset of one reference field, ascending (those of nested structs and fixed-size arrays included) |

Labels are `d1`, `d2`, … in order of first reference by an instruction of `sea.lir1` (file
order); every occurrence in the source has its own label (no sharing), except that a `slay`
record exists once per struct type: its label is given at the first reference to it, and every
later reference uses that label. Two label rules hold for `sea.lir1` only (L-bu): the numbering by
first reference, and that every defined label is referenced. In `sea.lir2` and `sea.lir` a defined
label may be unreferenced (T10 deletes `la` instructions, and the labels and data records are kept,
below) and the labels need not follow first reference; every other rule holds there too: labels
`d1`, `d2`, … defined in order with no gap, each referenced label defined, the data records after
the last function in label order. `lirrw`'s reader applies the two rules only when it reads
`sea.lir1` (in `seaopt`), not `sea.lir2` (in `sealopt`). The label limit `SEA_LIM_LIR_LABELS` is a
capacity limit (`TOO_LARGE`, `… labels`) only on `sea.lir1` input: pass 3b keeps every label, so
no `sea.lir2` or `sea.lir` can hold a label number above it, and a data label number above it in
such a file, defined or referenced, is a malformed record (`BAD_RECORD`, as `seaval` reports it),
never the user error `TOO_LARGE` (L-bv). Pass 4 already accepts this: `seagen_a64`
and `seagen_x64` check only that the labels are defined in order without a gap and that every
label an `la` names is defined, as they did on `seaopt`'s `sea.lir` before 5c-2; `seaval`'s format
`lir` already omits the two rules, and its format `lir2` must too (it is "checked as `lir1`" in all
else).

**Constant data of dynamic array literals** (phase 4). A `dat` buffer has no header (§4.8), so it
is never an array object: a dynamic array literal (LANGUAGE.md §6.9) is a fresh array at each
evaluation, which pass 3a allocates and fills (§3.6.6 rule 26), copying the elements from a `dat`
buffer with `mcopy` when every element is a numeric or `bool` constant. Sea has no static array
objects. Pass 3b keeps the labels
and every data record of its input, even one no instruction refers to any more. The data records
come in label order, after the last function. How pass 4 lays them out is fixed in `rt.inc`
(§4.8).

#### 3.6.3 Functions

```
func <name> <kind> <pos> <np> <params…> <nr> <classes…>
slot <s> <size> <align>                      0 or more stack slots
<instructions>
endfunc
```

| Record | Fields | Meaning |
|--------|--------|---------|
| `func` | `name:s kind:lkind pos:pos np:u par:reg*np nr:u cls:rcls*nr` | kind `main` (named `.main`, called by the runtime as `_sea_main`, §4.5) or `fn`; `pos` that of the HIR `fn` record (§3.5.4), which passes 3b and 4 report for a capacity limit (§2.6.2, `at` word `here`); parameters as registers; the classes of the results |
| `slot` | `id:slot size:u align:u` | a stack slot of `size` bytes, `align` a power of two; `s1`, `s2`, … in order |
| `endfunc` | — | the end of the function |

Functions come in the order of `sea.hir`, without those that pass 3a inlined completely
(elemental functions are always inlined, LANGUAGE.md §8.5, so no instance or elemental function
is ever a LIR function; neither is a prelude function, §3.6.4, "Sites"). Pass 4 chooses each function's assembler symbol (local to `sea.s`) except
for `.main`.

**Calling convention between Sea functions** (pass 4 maps it to AAPCS64 or the System V ABI):
`i64` and `bool` parameters and results are `i`, `f64` are `f`, `str`, arrays and handles are `p`
(the callee borrows them: it neither retains nor releases them, §4.2). A struct or fixed-size
array parameter is a `p` to the caller's memory, read-only for the callee. A `ref` parameter is a
`p` to the caller's variable in memory (a scalar `ref` argument lives in a stack slot of the caller
for the call). A struct or fixed-size array result is written by the callee to memory whose
address the caller passes as an extra parameter in front of the others, one per such result in
result order; it is not a register result. Several results are several result registers. A
`tret` (§3.5.5) is a `call` whose register results are returned by a `ret` of the same
registers; for results returned in memory, the function passes its own hidden result addresses
on to the callee in their place. LIR needs no record of its own for it.

#### 3.6.4 Instructions

The destination comes first. Operands are registers; constants are loaded with `li`/`lf`.
"site" is the `site` field (§3.1) of the source line an instruction's run-time error reports.

| Instruction | Operands | Meaning |
|-------------|----------|---------|
| `li` | `d:ri v:i` | load an `i64` constant |
| `lf` | `d:rf v:f` | load an `f64` constant (its exact bits) |
| `la` | `d:rp lab:lab` | the address of a data item |
| `sa` | `d:rp slot:slot` | the address of a stack slot |
| `mov` | `d:reg a:reg` | copy; both of the same class |
| `iadd isub imul` | `d:ri a:ri b:ri` | wrapping (mod 2⁶⁴); only where no overflow can occur (addresses, induction values) or wrapping is intended (magic division) |
| `iaddc isubc imulc` | `d:ri a:ri b:ri site:site` | exact; a result outside `i64` is `integer overflow` (LANGUAGE.md §6.5) |
| `ineg` | `d:ri a:ri` | negation, wrapping |
| `inegc` | `d:ri a:ri site:site` | negation, checked (`integer overflow`) |
| `idivf imodf` | `d:ri a:ri b:ri site:site` | floored quotient and modulo (LANGUAGE.md §6.6): a zero divisor is `integer division by zero`; `idivf` of −2⁶³ by −1 is `integer overflow` |
| `imulh` | `d:ri a:ri b:ri` | the high 64 bits of the signed 128-bit product |
| `iand ior ixor` | `d:ri a:ri b:ri` | bitwise |
| `ishl ishr isar` | `d:ri a:ri b:ri` | shift left, logical right, arithmetic right by the second operand (0 … 63) |
| `bnot` | `d:ri a:ri` | 1 if the operand is 0, else 0 |
| `icmp` | `cc:cc d:ri a:ri b:ri` | 1 if the signed comparison holds, else 0; cc `eq ne lt le gt ge` |
| `isel` | `d:ri c:ri a:ri b:ri` | d = a if c ≠ 0, else b |
| `fsel` | `d:rf c:ri a:rf b:rf` | the same for `f64` |
| `psel` | `d:rp c:ri a:rp b:rp` | the same for addresses |
